encounters.cc: Management of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus despite adherence to dietary modifications and regular exercise for the past 6 months.

lines: Management of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus despite adherence to dietary modifications and regular exercise for the past 6 months.

The patient with diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and CAD returns to endocrinology following January 2020 internal medicine care despite adherence to dietary modifications and regular exercise for past 6 months.
He was diagnosed 2 years ago and initially managed with metformin, which he tolerates well.
He has no history of hypoglycemic episodes.
His medical history is notable for hypertension and dyslipidemia.
His current medications are metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 64, Hypertension
He does not smoke or drink alcohol.
BMI of 31 kg/m² and blood pressure of 134/78 mm Hg
Fundoscopic examination reveals no diabetic retinopathy.
Hemoglobin A1c of 8.2%, fasting plasma glucose of 165 mg/dL, and a serum creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL
The decision is made to add an oral hypoglycemic agent that increases pancreatic β-cell insulin secretion by binding to and inhibiting ATP-dependent potassium channels on the β-cell membrane.

encounters.cc: Several months of worsening weakness in his dominant right hand causing difficulty with carpentry tools and dropping small objects.

lines: Several months of worsening weakness in his dominant right hand causing difficulty with carpentry tools and dropping small objects.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with coronary artery disease, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus previously evaluated in Internal Medicine and Endocrinology for blood pressure and glycemic management, who presents with several months of worsening weakness in his dominant right hand.

He works as a carpenter and has noticed increasing difficulty using his tools, particularly when trying to hold small nails between his fingers or when stabilizing pieces of wood that require hand dexterity.
He frequently drops screws or washers, especially when trying to pick them up with his ring and little fingers.
Over time, he has also observed a slow but progressive shrinkage of the muscles between his fingers and around the base of his little finger.
He initially thought it was due to aging and overuse, but now it is beginning to interfere with his work and daily functioning.
He denies pain, trauma, or systemic symptoms but does report intermittent numbness and tingling in the medial hand that worsens with prolonged elbow flexion or when resting his arm on a hard surface.
He sleeps with his arms bent under his pillow, and he sometimes notices hand numbness in the morning that resolves after a few minutes.
At work, he frequently leans his elbows against counters and tool benches.
He has tried wearing a wrist splint at night without significant benefit.
He has not seen any change in his grip strength while shaking hands or squeezing with his palm but finds tasks requiring finger spreading or pinching between fingers increasingly difficult.
He also notes trouble playing guitar, especially forming chords that require abducting and adducting individual fingers.
He has no symptoms in his left hand and no known history of neck problems.
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 64, Hypertension
He does not smoke and drinks socially
On physical exam, there is marked wasting of the hypothenar eminence and the first dorsal interosseous muscle on the right.
The hand shows mild clawing of the fourth and fifth digits at rest.
Strength testing reveals weakness in finger abduction and adduction, most noticeable when asked to spread his fingers against resistance or hold a piece of paper between the fingers.
Sensation is reduced over the palmar and dorsal surfaces of the fifth digit and the medial half of the fourth digit.
Grip strength is mildly reduced but wrist flexion, elbow strength, and forearm pronation/supination are intact.
Tinel sign is positive at the right elbow.
The physician explains that the pattern of sensory and motor findings indicates damage to a specific nerve supplying most of the intrinsic hand muscles.

encounters.cc: Intermittent chest pain described as pressure-like sensation over the left chest radiating to the left arm during morning walks for the past two months.

lines: Intermittent chest pain described as pressure-like sensation over the left chest radiating to the left arm during morning walks for the past two months.
This patient with coronary artery disease, hypertension, and diabetes presents to cardiology with chest pain.
The pain is described as a pressure-like sensation over the left chest, radiating to the left arm, and occurs during his morning walks.
He denies any symptoms at rest.
- Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (Cubital tunnel syndrome) (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
His current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin.
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 64, Hypertension
Smoking: Former smoker, 18 pack-years, quit 3 months ago.
His blood pressure is 138/86 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, and BMI is 30 kg/m^2.
Subsequent coronary angiography reveals a 70% stenosis of the left anterior descending artery.
An exercise stress test shows ST-segment depression in the anterior leads at high levels of exertion.
The patient is enrolled in a clinical trial comparing a new anti-anginal medication to placebo.
After 6 months, the trial results show a p-value of 0.008 for the difference in exercise tolerance between the new medication and placebo.

encounters.cc: Abrupt onset of double vision that started this morning.

lines: Abrupt onset of double vision that started this morning.
The patient, with longstanding type 2 diabetes and prior emergency department evaluation, is brought to the emergency department because of double vision that started abruptly this morning.
- Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (Cubital tunnel syndrome) (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
He has a history of poorly controlled hypertension and diabetes mellitus.
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 64, Hypertension
Smoking: Former smoker, 18 pack-years, quit 3 months ago.
On examination, his right eye is deviated down and out at rest, and he is unable to adduct or elevate that eye.
The right pupil is dilated and poorly reactive to light.
He has intact sensation over the face and normal visual acuity.
His lacrimal reflex is preserved bilaterally.
The physician suspects a cranial nerve palsy.
